items.followUp: What is the purpose of the <UL> tag in HTML?

rubric.why: Identifies what OL stands for or creates.
rubric.description: States that OL creates an ordered list.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying an ordered or numbered list.

rubric.why: Explains how an ordered list is displayed.
rubric.description: States that list items are shown in a numbered or otherwise ordered sequence.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing the ordered numbering of its items.

modelAnswer: The <OL> (Ordered List) tag is used to create an ordered list in an HTML document.
Its list items are displayed in sequence, usually with numbers.

items.followUp: Differentiate between an HTML link and a URL.

rubric.why: Checks that the student explains the function of a hyperlink.
rubric.description: A hyperlink is a clickable link that takes the user to another page, file, or resource.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing a hyperlink as a clickable connection to another destination.

rubric.why: Checks that the student distinguishes an anchor from a hyperlink.
rubric.description: An anchor identifies a location or target in a document; a hyperlink can point to that target.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying an anchor as a named location or target, including one within the same page.

modelAnswer: A hyperlink is a clickable connection that takes the user to another webpage, file, or resource.
An anchor identifies a specific location or target in a webpage; a hyperlink can be used to jump to that location.

items.followUp: Explain normal, invalid, boundary, and extreme test data.

rubric.why: Checks understanding of data that should be accepted during testing.
rubric.description: Normal test data is valid data that is expected to be accepted by the program.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for defining normal or valid test data.

rubric.why: Checks understanding of tests near the allowed range.
rubric.description: Boundary test data checks values at or near the limits of the acceptable range.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying values at or near the acceptable limits.

rubric.why: Checks understanding of data that should be rejected.
rubric.description: Invalid or erroneous test data does not meet the program's rules and should be rejected.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for defining invalid or erroneous data.

rubric.why: Checks understanding of testing at the furthest valid values.
rubric.description: Extreme test data uses the highest or lowest values within the acceptable range.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying extreme values as the highest or lowest valid values.

modelAnswer: Normal test data: valid, typical data that the program is expected to accept.
Boundary test data: values at or near the limits of the acceptable range.
Invalid (erroneous) test data: data that breaks the rules and should be rejected.
Extreme test data: the highest or lowest values within the acceptable range.

items.followUp: Define a communication channel and give one example.

rubric.why: Checks the meaning of a communication system.
rubric.description: Defines a communication system as a system for sending or exchanging information between entities.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a definition involving the exchange or transmission of information.

rubric.why: Checks identification of a key system component.
rubric.description: The sender or source initiates and sends the message.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming and explaining the sender/source.

rubric.why: Checks identification of the path used to carry information.
rubric.description: The medium or channel carries the message from sender to receiver.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming and explaining the medium/channel.

rubric.why: Checks identification of the entity that gets the message.
rubric.description: The receiver or destination receives the message.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming and explaining the receiver/destination.

modelAnswer: A communication system is a system that sends or exchanges information between two or more entities.
Sender: the source that creates and sends the message.
Medium: the channel through which the message travels.
Receiver: the destination that receives the message.

items.followUp: What is malware? State three ways it can harm a computer user.

rubric.why: Checks the definition and purpose of a phishing attack.
rubric.description: Phishing is a fraudulent attempt to impersonate a trusted source and trick users into revealing sensitive information.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing a deceptive attempt to obtain sensitive information.

rubric.why: Checks recognition of a common phishing-email warning sign.
rubric.description: The email may use urgent or threatening language to pressure the recipient.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying urgency or pressure as a characteristic.

rubric.why: Checks recognition of suspicious links or attachments.
rubric.description: The email may contain a suspicious link or attachment that leads to a fake site or harmful content.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying a suspicious link or attachment.

rubric.why: Checks recognition of requests for confidential details.
rubric.description: The email may ask for passwords, financial details, or other personal information.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying a request for sensitive information.

modelAnswer: A phishing attack is a fraudulent attempt to impersonate a trusted person or organisation to trick users into revealing sensitive information.
A phishing email may use urgent or threatening language to pressure the recipient.
It may contain suspicious links or attachments.
It may ask the recipient for passwords, financial details, or other personal information.

rubric.why: Checks the first division and remainder in the repeated-division method.
rubric.description: Divides 999 by 16 to obtain quotient 62 and remainder 7.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct quotient and remainder.

rubric.why: Checks the hexadecimal digits in reverse remainder order.
rubric.description: Gives the final hexadecimal answer as (3E7)₁₆.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct final answer.

modelAnswer: Given: (999)₁₀
999 ÷ 16 = 62 remainder 7
62 ÷ 16 = 3 remainder 14 = E
3 ÷ 16 = 0 remainder 3
Read the remainders from bottom to top: (999)₁₀ = (3E7)₁₆.

items.followUp: What does the problem-solving strategy 'break it down' mean?

rubric.why: Checks the central action in the strategy.
rubric.description: Act It Out means physically performing or representing the steps of a problem.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that the problem is acted or physically represented.

rubric.why: Checks the purpose of using the strategy.
rubric.description: The activity helps make the problem or its steps easier to understand and solve.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that acting it out helps understand or solve the problem.

modelAnswer: Act It Out is a problem-solving strategy in which the situation or steps of a problem are physically performed or represented.
It helps make the problem easier to understand and solve.

items.followUp: What is verification in data processing?

rubric.why: Checks that validation involves checking data.
rubric.description: Validation is the process of checking input data.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying validation as a check on data.

rubric.why: Checks what the data is checked against.
rubric.description: The check determines whether data meets specified rules or is within an acceptable range.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for referring to rules, reasonableness, or an acceptable range.

modelAnswer: Validation is the process of checking input data to ensure that it follows specified rules and is within an acceptable range.
